correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier expansion gives the full finite-circle angular Hessian. The Taylor coefficient has an exact alias-residue form S_k-S_0; applying Fourier transform to x² exp(-2 t x²) proves the fine-time positive exponential prefactor and first-mode ordering, while minimal-norm representatives of residue classes prove the coarse-time Nyquist ordering. The nonrotational branches are continuous and must exchange. Normalizations were checked against independently computed finite differences (134 supplemental assertions); computations do not replace infinite-sum proof.

value.rationale: The first scale-sensitive, fully modal local condition spectrum for geometric heat effective sample size on an intrinsically periodic sample geometry identifies an unavoidable change of the least-stable geometric deformation for every N>=4. Exact exponential fine-scale and spectral coarse-scale curvatures tell how robust a regular sampling design is to angular displacements; this is a motivated stability/design invariant rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. It does not require an all-scale global optimization theorem.
